i want to start a online english language school, my wife is an english teacher and i have tech skills, i need an actionable buisness plan . I tend to have to many ideas but get distracted and overwhelmed. i need step by step guidance to get this off the ground and make income fast.

You can totally do this, *as long as you keep it small and focused at the start*. Let’s build you a “money-first” launch plan instead of a giant overwhelming project.

I’ll break it into:

1. Ground rules so you don’t get overwhelmed  
2. One clear business model (fastest way to cash)  
3. A 30-day step-by-step launch plan  
4. Scripts \+ concrete actions to get your first students

---

## **1\. Ground rules (so you don’t drown in ideas)**

For the next 30 days:

* One offer only  
  No apps, no giant platform, no 10 different programs. One simple offer that your wife can teach and you can deliver with basic tools.  
* One main channel to get clients  
  E.g., local WhatsApp / Facebook groups \+ your personal contacts. No SEO, no blog, no YouTube (yet).  
* Idea parking lot  
  When you get a new idea, write it in a note called “Later” and *do not* act on it this month.  
* Daily 45–60 min “needle-moving” block  
  Every day you either:  
  * talk to potential students, or  
  * improve the offer/lesson experience for existing ones.

Nothing else matters as much early on.  
---

## **2\. Simple business model: what you’ll actually sell**

Fastest way to income: live Zoom lessons with a premium but simple package.

Pick *one* of these to start (my recommendation is \#2):

1. 1:1 “English Upgrade” coaching (teens/adults)  
   * 8 x 60-min lessons over 4 weeks  
   * Focus: speaking confidence \+ real life situations (work, travel, school).  
   * Higher price per student, easy to customize.  
2. Small group “Boost Your English” course (6–10 learners) ← *Recommended*  
   * 4–6 weeks, 2 lessons per week, 60 minutes each.  
   * Age group: very specific (e.g., “5th–7th grade kids who need homework \+ speaking help” or “Adults B1–B2 who want speaking confidence”).  
   * Same lesson taught to everyone \= efficient.  
3. Homework Club / Exam Prep Club (kids/teens)  
   * 2–3 sessions per week where kids bring their homework, your wife leads structured help \+ speaking practice.  
   * Great for Israeli kids / local market.

### **Quick money math (example)**

Let’s say you offer a 6-week Small Group Course:

* Price: 600 ₪ per student (example)  
* 2 lessons per week → 12 live lessons total  
* Group size: 8 students

Income from one group:  
600 ₪ × 8 \= 4,800 ₪ for 6 weeks

Run two groups (different times):  
≈ 9,600 ₪ in 6 weeks

That’s *already* a real business. No fancy tech.  
---

## **3\. Your 30-day launch plan**

### **Week 1 – Decide \+ Prepare (No marketing yet)**

Goal: Choose niche \+ offer, set price, prep basic materials.

Day 1–2 – Choose niche & outcome

Answer these quickly (don’t overthink):

1. Who is your first target?  
   * Option A: Israeli school kids who need English help  
   * Option B: Adults who want speaking confidence  
   * Option C: Professionals (hi-tech, nurses, etc.)  
2. What is the clear promise for 4–6 weeks?  
   * e.g., “Your child will feel confident doing English homework and speaking in class.”  
   * or: “You’ll be able to hold a 10-minute conversation in English about everyday topics without freezing.”

Write one sentence:

“I help \[WHO\] go from \[POINT A\] to \[POINT B\] in \[TIME\].”  
---

Day 3 – Define your offer

Decide:

* Format:  
  * 1:1 or small group? (Pick one)  
  * How many weeks? (4–6 is great)  
  * How many sessions per week? (1–2)  
* What they get:  
  * Live Zoom lessons  
  * Homework or practice tasks  
  * Simple feedback via WhatsApp/email

Write it clearly, e.g.:

“6-week small group course · 2x/week on Zoom · max 8 students · homework support \+ speaking practice · parents get weekly progress message.”  
---

Day 4 – Set your price

For fast income, don’t undercharge.

* 4–6 week small group:  
  * Anywhere from 500–800 ₪ per student is reasonable for high-touch, live classes.  
* 1:1 program (8 sessions):  
  * 1,200–2,000 ₪ per student depending on your confidence & target market.

Pick one price and stick with it this month. You can always raise later.  
---

Day 5–7 – Set up the basics (no website needed)

Keep it stupid simple:

* Tools:  
  1. Zoom or Google Meet  
  2. WhatsApp for communication  
  3. Google Docs/Slides for materials  
  4. Payment: Bit, PayBox, bank transfer, or credit card (whatever you already use)  
* Make:  
  1. A one-page Google Doc / PDF explaining your offer:  
     * Who it’s for  
     * What problem it solves  
     * What’s included (number of lessons, days/times, group size)  
     * Price \+ payment method  
     * Start date  
  2. A simple intake form (Google Form):  
     * Student’s name \+ age/level  
     * Parent’s name (if kid)  
     * WhatsApp number  
     * Their main goal/struggle

You can send me your niche and I can draft that whole one-pager \+ form for you next.  
---

### **Week 2 – Get your first 3–10 paying students**

Goal: Fill your first group / book first 1:1 slots.

You’ll focus on warm audience first: people who already know/trust you (friends, parents at your kids’ school, your wife’s colleagues, WhatsApp groups, shul community, etc.).

#### **Step A – Personal outreach (most important)**

You \+ your wife each message 10–20 people.

Sample WhatsApp message:

Hey \[Name\] 😊  
\[Wife’s name\] and I are opening a small online English program for \[kids grade/ adults level\].  
It’s a 6-week live Zoom course, max 8 students, focused on \[homework help / speaking confidence / exam prep\].  
We’re starting on \[DATE\] and I thought of you because \[your child is in that age group / you mentioned wanting better English for work\].

Would you like the details?

If they say yes, send your one-pager \+ intake form.

Do *not* send a mass spammy message. Always make it slightly personal.

#### **Step B – Two or three posts in groups**

Post in:

* Local neighborhood / city groups  
* Parents groups (by grade/ school)  
* English learning / Olim groups (if relevant)

Sample post:

🎓 NEW small online English group for \[5th–7th graders\]

My wife is an experienced English teacher and we’re opening a small Zoom group (max 8 kids) for 6 weeks, starting \[DATE\].

✅ Help with school homework  
✅ Speaking practice in a fun, low-stress way  
✅ Weekly update for parents on progress

2 lessons per week · 60 minutes · \[DAY & TIME OPTIONS\]

If you want details, comment “info” or message me directly.

Keep it simple, friendly, not salesy.  
---

### **Week 3 – Deliver & improve (while still selling)**

Goal: Start teaching your first group / 1:1 students and make it amazing.

* Teach Week 1 lessons.  
* After each lesson, ask yourself:  
  * What confused them?  
  * What did they enjoy?  
  * Where did they struggle?  
* Send a short follow-up message to parents/adults:

“Hi \[Name\], today we worked on \[topic\]. \[Student\] did really well with \[X\] and we’ll keep practicing \[Y\].”

This builds insane trust and makes referrals much easier.

Keep posting once a week about:

* Progress of your group (no names)  
* A small English tip  
* A reminder that people can join next round / book 1:1.

---

### **Week 4 – Fill next group & raise price (optional)**

By now you should have:

* A working offer  
* Testimonials (even 1–2 sentences from parents / adult students)  
* More clarity on what students actually need

Use that to:

* Open registration for Group \#2 with a clear start date  
* Slightly raise your price (e.g. from 600 → 700 ₪)  
* Decide whether to add:  
  * Another group, or  
  * Limited number of 1:1 spots at a higher price

---

## **4\. How you and your wife divide roles**

Use your strengths:

* Your wife (teacher):  
  * Lesson planning & teaching  
  * Assessment of level  
  * Giving feedback to students/parents  
* You (tech \+ biz):  
  * Set up forms, Zoom links, simple landing page later  
  * Payments & tracking who paid / which group they’re in  
  * Marketing messages, group posts, WhatsApp outreach  
  * Long term: maybe LMS, simple website, automations

Think of yourself as the “school director \+ tech”, she’s the “head teacher”.  
---

# **✅ Recommended Structure (High-Commitment \+ Easy to Sell)**

## **Group 1: Younger Kids (Ages 6–9)**

* Parents LOVE the frequency → it feels like “real progress”  
* Kids bond with the teacher faster  
* Easier for parents to justify the monthly fee  
* Very little resistance

380–420 ₪ per month  
(Parents happily pay this for 2x/week English)  
---

## **Group 2: Older Kids (Ages 10–12)**

→ 1 longer lesson per week (55–60 min)

Why this works:

* Older kids tolerate longer sessions  
* Less scheduling complexity  
* Very easy to market (“just one strong weekly lesson”)  
* Parents see this age as “more serious academically”

Price recommendation:  
280–350 ₪ per month  
---

# **🎯 Why this combo is the sweet spot**

### **Fast to fill**

* Younger groups fill because parents see English as essential  
* Older groups fill because it’s a low-commitment time investment

### **Easier for YOU**

* Your wife can reuse the same materials year-round  
* You can run 1–2 younger groups \+ 1–2 older groups → solid income  
* Predictable schedule  
* Easy to add new students monthly

### **Higher retention**

Parents stick for the whole year because:

* Kids enjoy frequent short lessons → younger group  
* Older kids like routine and clear progress

### **Better quality experience**

* Small groups  
* Clear goals (reading, writing fluency)  
* Kids see improvement weekly → parents stay long-term

# **📚 6\. Month 1 Curriculum Outline (Starter)**

## **Ages 6–9 (2×/week)**

Week 1 – Building Confidence

* Phonics warmups  
* Sight words  
* Short reading passages  
* Fun writing: “My favorite…” sentences

Week 2 – Reading Fluency

* Short story reading  
* Echo reading & choral reading  
* Writing: 3–5 sentence paragraph

Week 3 – Vocabulary Growth

* Themed vocabulary (animals, hobbies)  
* Reading comprehension questions  
* Writing: simple descriptions

Week 4 – Putting It Together

* Story of the week  
* Reading games  
* Writing: beginning/middle/end story

---

## **Ages 10–12 (1×/week)**

Week 1 – Reading Skills

* Main idea / details  
* Short story analysis  
* Writing: topic sentence \+ supporting sentences

Week 2 – Writing Structure

* Using transitions: first, then, next  
* Summary writing  
* Vocabulary exercises

Week 3 – Grammar \+ Writing

* Present/Past tense review  
* Writing: personal letter / short essay  
* Reading response

Week 4 – Fluency

* Longer reading passage  
* Paragraph writing  
* Editing \+ rewriting for clarity

# **5️⃣ Month 1 Curriculum (FULLY FINALISED)**

(Already matched to your pedagogical structure in earlier project chats)

### **Level 1 (Ages 6–9):**

WEEK 1

* Story: “Charlie the Curious Cat”  
* Phonics: C / K / S review  
* Reading: CVC words  
* Writing: “I like…” sentences  
* Game: Circle-the-sound

WEEK 2

* Story: “Milo the Mouse’s Big Day”  
* Reading: short passages  
* Writing: 3-sentence paragraph  
* Recognition task: Find-the-word  
* Craft extension (optional)

WEEK 3

* Story: “Luna’s Lost Balloon”  
* Vocabulary: feelings  
* Writing: sentence expansion  
* Reading: echo reading  
* Game: WordPet Bingo

WEEK 4

* Story: “Pip’s Picnic Adventure”  
* Reading comprehension  
* Writing: beginning/middle/end  
* Game: Reading Race  
* Optional: Printable storybook

---

### **Level 2 (Ages 10–12):**

WEEK 1

* Reading: short article  
* Writing: topic sentence  
* Grammar: Present simple/past simple  
* Response paragraph

WEEK 2

* Reading: story excerpt  
* Writing: transitions  
* Editing skills  
* Vocabulary in context

WEEK 3

* Reading: informational text  
* Writing: descriptive paragraph  
* Grammar: fragments/run-ons  
* Independent task

WEEK 4

* Reading: extended passage  
* Writing: short essay draft  
* Editing and rewriting  
* Parent progress report

---

# **🥇 1\. Nearpod (Best overall for kids 6–12)**

**![https://nearpod.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Student-Teacher-View.png][image1]**

**![https://nearpod.zendesk.com/hc/article\_attachments/7790360257172][image2]**

**![https://nearpod.zendesk.com/hc/article\_attachments/360069979692][image3]**

6

### **✔ What it gives you:**

* Upload slides, video, images, audio narration  
* Built-in games (matching, memory, time-to-climb game, drawing, polls)  
* Students join with a code  
* Works perfectly for Zoom lessons (teacher-paced mode)  
* Amazing for ages 6–12

### **⭐ Why it's the best for your use-case:**

* The interactive games feel like mini WordPets activities  
* Super easy to repeat weekly routines  
* Parents LOVE how structured it looks  
* You can store your stories \+ audio in one lesson

### **💰 Price:**

Free tier is good enough to start.  
Paid (if needed): \~$10–15/month.

Most recommended for your program.

* Story-based
